title: Speaking through the Eyes
paragraphs: The confidant was hiding beside the bushes for a long time Without causing any embarrassment to the lovers rendezvousing; He put a stop even to his cough That tended to come out of this throat, For that was not the hour to do so.
He was all ears to listen to what they were speaking. There was no sound to be heard.
“Where have they gone? Are they present or not?” Confusion reigned over his head.
He stretched up a little, Both of them were seen standing like statues.
What is the need for language, when the two eyes are there? They knew it well that
Of no avail whatever are words of mouth Where eyes meet eyes in acquiescence true.

The love which was like a flower has now grown into a green fruit. They knew that in keeping with the Tamil ethos, They should wait till their love turned into a ripe fruit. That is the way of the Tamils prescribed in Tolkāppiyam.
“The union of two hearts is not a short story. I convey my greetings for it to become a never-ending saga; Depart for the day and come tomorrow.” So said the genial friend.
Since it was time for the devotees to throng the temple, They decided that the day’s converse of the eyes was enough and parted.
The confidant clutched the shoulder of the hero and said, “The woman is a beauty endowed with timidity, bashfulness and credulity.”

The hero intervened and corrected the friend’s note: “The dame fell into fear as I touched her; Bashfulness is an inborn virtue unto women, And I don’t accept ignorance in women. If both of us were given to ignorance Wouldn’t it lead to physical relationship?
We the birds of love Have a perfect understanding that The clandestine career is one Where the hearts unite With no room for fleshly congress, And so we parted after our hearts united into one.”
After the hero finished his address The bosom friend responded with his eyes pulled wide apart in amazement: “You have conveyed your passion By signs healthy And by a language unspoken Thereby
Fortifying male resolve and female reserve! May each day of your rendezvous Be as blessed as this day’s!” The confidant greeted the hero thus In keeping with the Tamil culture.

> The meeting of eyes is the pointer sure > Suggesting the union of minds. > > Where the glances of the eyes reciprocate, > There marks the sprouting of a love career, > So has it been said. > > Nobility of bearing and fortitude > Are such stuff as marks the male [hero]. > > Timidity, bashfulness and credulity > Are the ruling traits in a woman [heroine]. > > (Poruḷatikāram : Kaḷaviyal, verses 5, 6, 7, 8)
